subject: Reservation granularity & heartbeat window: product + ops coordination
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: EdgePilot Ops <ops@edgepilot.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@edgepilot.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reservation granularity & heartbeat window: product + ops coordination

Hi all —

Quick context: EdgePilot is planning a model sweep (A/B + two large quantized variants) across their pilot fleet the week of Apr 18. They asked for a dedicated reservation with finer-grain slots (15-minute slices) and a longer heartbeat window so their long-running orchestration doesn’t get preempted while iterating.

Ask for the Redwood side: can we make a one-off exception to allow 15-minute reservation granularity for this reservation and extend the heartbeat to 10 minutes for the duration of the run? They estimate ~280 concurrent endpoints for a 48–72 hour window.

Notes attached: reservation_delta_model-run-plan.xlsx (forecast, expected token volumes), and I’ll attach the exemption form once legal approves.

What I need from ops/infra/product:
- Ops: feasibility and impact (fragmentation, eviction risk)
- Infra: any scheduler or autoscale constraints that block 15-minute granularity or 10-minute heartbeat
- Product: approval criteria, rollback triggers, and customer commitments (SLA addendum?)

Would like to land a decision by EOD Wed so EdgePilot can confirm scheduling.

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reservation_delta_model-run-plan.xlsx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reservation granularity & heartbeat window: product + ops coordination

Tessa —

Thanks for the summary. A few immediate questions:

1) Forecast accuracy: the attachment gives peaks but not distribution. Are the 280 endpoints constant or bursty? If bursty, what is peak concurrency and median?
2) Priority: do we treat EdgePilot as preemptible pilot traffic or a hard reservable customer for this window?
3) Alternatives: we can either (A) carve out a contiguous reservation (coarse but isolated) or (B) permit fine-grain 15-min slices routed through a priority band. Option B increases scheduler fragmentation but preserves general pool availability.

From ops perspective I need the forecast numbers by EOD Tue to size buffer. If we go with 15-min granularity we should limit to one region and attach eviction triggers (error rate > X or latency degrad > Y) to auto-release.

I’ll loop John from capacity planning if we need to shift slices across pools.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Dedicated Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reservation granularity & heartbeat window: product + ops coordination

Kim / Tessa —

Technical constraints to flag:
- Scheduler minimum slot is currently 30 minutes for dedicated GPUs due to our slab allocation model. Moving to 15-minute slices will double fragmentation and increases background scheduling churn by ~2.1x based on recent simulations.
- Heartbeat extension to 10 minutes is workable but needs additional lease-holding changes: currently kube-proxy times out at 5m for stale KV tokens; we can extend to 10m but must ship a small release (infra flag) and monitor KV pressure. Estimated work: 1 engineer day + smoke tests.
- If EdgePilot runs 48–72 hours at ~280 concurrent, we need to reserve ~4.5x their 95th percentile token throughput as a buffer to avoid tail latency regressions.

Mitigations:
- Limit 15-minute granularity to a single GPU pool (us-west) to contain fragmentation.
- Add auto-release triggers: error-rate > 3% for 10 minutes OR sustained 90th-percentile latency > 2s for model endpoints.

I can prototype the heartbeat flag tomorrow; we’ll need ops to sign off on the pool carve and release timeline.

-Dev
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reservation granularity & heartbeat window: product + ops coordination

On Apr 4, 2027, at 11:03 AM, Kimberly Park wrote:
> Tessa —
> 
> Thanks for the summary. A few immediate questions:
> 
> 1) Forecast accuracy: the attachment gives peaks but not distribution. Are the 280 endpoints constant or bursty?

Quick response from product side: EdgePilot’s orchestrator will spin up endpoints as they get tranche results; they expect stepwise increases but not full fanout immediately. Practically we should plan for a ramp to 280 over ~6 hours with intermittent peaks.

Product proposal: we accept a temporary exception under the following terms —
- Duration: 72 hours starting Apr 18 00:00 PDT.
- Scope: us-west pool only.
- Reservation: 15-minute granularity allowed for this reservation id.
- Heartbeat: extended to 10 minutes.
- Release policy: ops can revoke reservation early if auto-release triggers fire.
- Customer commitment: EdgePilot signs addendum agreeing to pay for allocated reservation and to follow release triggers.

Rollback triggers (immediate release):
- Sustained >5% error rate across endpoints for 15 minutes
- Pool-level 95th tail latency increases by >30% for >10 minutes

If everyone is aligned I’ll draft the customer-facing addendum and the short runbook for ops.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Group Product Manager — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

All —

From a customer-ops and procurement angle: we can support this exception but need two items before booking:
1) Signed exemption form (attached) — cap-exemption-request-form.pdf
2) A short SLA addendum that limits our liability during the extended-heartbeat window and clarifies preemption behavior.

EdgePilot has verbally agreed to the terms but wants confirmation that we won’t preempt their endpoints mid-run. We need to be explicit: we reserve the right to preempt if rollback triggers hit. Please make sure the addendum language is clear.

I'll create a HubSpot deal note and an INF Jira ticket to track the carve. Linking both here: https://hubspot.com/contacts/EdgePilot-12345 and https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1289.

Thanks team —

We’re aligned. Action summary and next steps:
- Dev: prototype heartbeat flag and coordinate canary deployment in us-west by Apr 8.
- Ops (Kim): prepare a single us-west carve of 300 concurrency-equivalent slots for Apr 18 00:00 PDT through Apr 21 00:00 PDT. Mark reservation id: RSRV-EP-20270418-01.
- Product (Laura): draft customer addendum and runbook (include rollback triggers), deliver by Apr 9.
- Sales (Aditya): collect signed cap-exemption-request-form.pdf and customer signature on addendum; create HubSpot note and confirm billing commit.

EdgePilot: please review the appended run plan and sign the attached exemption form. Once we have signatures we’ll finalize the reservation and send the formal booking confirmation.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn here.
